extracted.intended_audience: public health practitioners, risk communicators, emergency responders, WHO country and partner staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and implementing risk communication, community engagement, and infodemic management during health emergencies so communities can make informed decisions and be equal partners in response. Covers principles, goals, unit roles, and practical toolkits for country-level readiness and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk communication as real-time exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication is the real-time exchange of information, advice and opinions between experts or officials and people who face a hazard or threat to their survival, health, or economic or social wellbeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes timeliness and two-way exchange (not one-way messaging). Applicable during hazards such as disease outbreaks. This principle underpins preparedness and response planning and should be enacted in operational settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: enable informed decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of risk communication is to enable people at risk to make informed decisions to mitigate the effects of a threat (hazard) – such as a disease outbreak – and take protective and preventive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All communications should be framed and evaluated by whether they help individuals and communities understand risks and take protective actions. Focus messaging on actionable guidance and decision support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement as equal partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Community engagement is the process of developing relationships and structures that engage communities as equal partners in the creation of emergency response solutions that are acceptable and workable for those they impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement must move beyond consultation to shared design and decision-making. Structures should enable communities to co-create response solutions rather than just receive instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empower communities to share leadership, planning and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of community engagement is to empower communities to confidently share the leadership, planning and implementation of initiatives throughout the health emergency response cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should build capacity for local leadership and ensure communities participate across preparedness, response and recovery phases. Measure success by degree of local ownership and leadership roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design solutions that are acceptable and workable for communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication and community engagement work to ensure that accurate information is delivered to communities in ways that are acceptable and workable for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt messages, channels, timing and activities to local norms, languages, and capacities. Avoid one-size-fits-all approaches; test acceptability and operational feasibility with community partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate risk communication into operational activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessons learned in risk communication and community engagement initiatives in every public health emergency have informed subsequent response efforts, leading to planning that better integrates risk communication into operational activities and brings communities to the forefront as valued and essential partners for effective, equitable and inclusive emergency preparedness and response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCCE should not be an add-on; it must be embedded in incident plans, surveillance, clinical response and logistics. Allocate staff, budget and processes to operationalize RCCE alongside technical interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-centered approach: local voices shape preparedness and response
rubrics_metrics.description: A key focus of the CPR Unit is fostering a community-centered approach to health emergencies, ensuring that local voices and priorities shape preparedness and response efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize listening, participatory needs assessments, and mechanisms for communities to set priorities. Tailor interventions to community-identified risks and preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accessible, evidence-based information and manage infodemics
rubrics_metrics.description: Through risk communication, community engagement, and infodemic management, the unit empowers communities with accessible, evidence-based information, enabling them to make informed decisions that protect their health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information must be accurate, understandable, and accessible across formats and languages. Active infodemic management (detecting and countering misinformation) is integral to RCCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop sustainable, community-led solutions tailored to diverse contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit works closely with governments, partners, and local communities to develop sustainable, community-led solutions tailored to diverse needs and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design interventions for long-term sustainability and adaptability. Co-develop solutions with a diversity lens and ensure they are appropriate for socioeconomic and cultural variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCCE as a core capacity in international frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication is a core capacity of the International Health Regulations (IHR 2005) and is one of five strategies within the Pandemic Influenza Preparedness (PIP) framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries are expected to build and maintain RCCE capacities to meet international obligations; planning and evaluation should reference IHR and PIP requirements where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of practical toolkits and context-specific readiness resources
rubrics_metrics.description: WHO provides risk communication and community engagement readiness and response toolkits (e.g., for mass gatherings, Ebola, Zika, dengue, mpox, yellow fever) to support country-level RCCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use and adapt WHO toolkits and readiness resources for specific hazards and settings. Toolkits provide practical steps, templates and resources to operationalize RCCE at country level; they should be localized and integrated into country plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from prior emergencies and continuously improve RCCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessons learned in risk communication and community engagement initiatives in every public health emergency have informed subsequent response efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and apply lessons learned, conduct after-action reviews, and update plans and materials accordingly to strengthen future preparedness and response.
